To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) ethical guidance for HIV vaccine trials in the form of ethical recommendations is generally well received by stakeholders in South Africa, and 2) ethical guidance for the prevention component of HIV vaccine trials is not well received by stakeholders.

“Stakeholders rated recommendations regarding care and prevention in HIV vaccine trial participants more highly than recommendations regarding informed consent. The most problematic recommendations were those related to prevention, especially those assigned low scores for ease of implementing.”
